import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 946

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/946](https://www.erdosproblems.com/946)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}.
   Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.
 - [Sp81] Spiro, C. A., The frequency with which an integral-valued, prime-independent,
   multiplicative or additive function of n divides a polynomial function of n.
 - [He84] Heath-Brown, D. R., The divisor function at consecutive integers.
   Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149.
 - [Hi85] Hildebrand, A., The divisor function at consecutive integers. Pacific J. Math.
   (1987), 307--319
 - [EPS87] Erdős, P., Pomerance, C., and Sarkőzy, A., On locally repeated values of
   arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/

open Filter Real
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos946

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. -/
noncomputable def erdos946Count (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter (fun n => σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1))).card

/--
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos946

findings.description: The docstring at lines 62–63 says the count is eventually at least x/(log x)^7, with coefficient 1. The Lean statement encodes a lower bound up to an unspecified positive constant: ∃ c > 0, ∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, c * (x/(log x)^7) ≤ erdos946Count x. The Lean statement matches the cited source; only the docstring omits the implicit constant.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/946 states Heath-Brown's bound as “≫ x/(log x)^7”. Hildebrand, The divisor function at consecutive integers, p. 307, equation (1.1), also quotes this bound with ≫: https://msp.org/pjm/1987/129-2/pjm-v129-n2-p06-s.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “at least c x/(log x)^7 for some constant c > 0 and all sufficiently large x”, or use Ω(x/(log x)^7). Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The module bibliography identifies [He84] as Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, pp. 141–149. The article appeared in issue 1, not issue 2. This does not affect any theorem statement.
findings.source_evidence: Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata for DOI 10.1112/S0025579300010743 records volume 31, issue 1, June 1984, pages 141–149: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1112%2FS0025579300010743.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “no. 2” with “no. 1” in the [He84] bibliography entry.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses a range starting at zero and a natural-valued floor, whereas the arithmetic counting function concerns positive integers n ≤ x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved that, for every real x and natural n, membership in the filtered range is equivalent to 0 < n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1). At n = 0 the equality fails because σ 0 0 = 0 and σ 0 1 = 1. For positive n, n ≤ ⌊x⌋₊ is equivalent to (n : ℝ) ≤ x, even when x is negative. Thus the count is exactly the intended count for every real x.

reformulations.difference: The source writes the count as ≫ x/(log x)^7; Lean instead places x/(log x)^7 on the left of =O[atTop].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved the Lean proposition equivalent to ∃ c > 0, ∃ X : ℝ, ∀ x ≥ X, c * (x/(log x)^7) ≤ erdos946Count x. Mathlib's Big-O definition supplies an eventual norm inequality; nonnegativity of the count and eventual positivity of the comparison function remove the norms. This is precisely the source's ≫ bound.

reformulations.difference: The source writes the count as ≫ x/(log log x)^3; Lean expresses this as x/(log log x)^3 =O[atTop] erdos946Count.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved equivalence to ∃ c > 0, ∃ X : ℝ, ∀ x ≥ X, c * (x/(log (log x))^3) ≤ erdos946Count x. Both functions are eventually nonnegative, so the Big-O norm inequality is exactly the asserted lower bound with a positive implicit constant. Hildebrand's abstract and Theorem 1 confirm the iterated logarithm and exponent 3.

No mathematical misformalizations were found, and all five research-solved tags agree with the current source. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings; it checks small divisor counts, both positive-shift predicates at zero, negative and fractional counting endpoints, square-root parsing, and explicit-constant equivalents of all three asymptotic bounds. These proofs do not use the reviewed file's sorry theorems. The original full texts of Heath-Brown's paper and Spiro's thesis were not obtained; their relevant results are explicitly stated both on the cited problem page and in Hildebrand's introduction, p. 307. The target file was not modified.
